results.quote: Directional mergesort sorts an array of size n with run-based entropy H using no more than nH+3n comparisons and 1.5nH+5n element moves. Excluding the merge buffer of size ⌈n/2⌉, the algorithm uses O(lg n) auxiliary words.

Directional mergesort sorts an array of size n with run-based entropy H using no more than nH+3n comparisons and 1.5nH+5n element moves. Excluding the merge buffer of size ⌈n/2⌉, the algorithm uses O(lg n) auxiliary words.
Directional mergesort++ sorts an array of size n containing r# runs in at most nH+3n-r# comparisons (where H is defined for both non-decreasing and decreasing runs).

Directional Mergesort++ sorts an array of size n with run-based entropy H (defined for both non-decreasing and decreasing runs) using no more than nH+3n comparisons and 1.5nH+6.5n moves. Excluding the merge buffer of size ⌈n/2⌉, the algorithm uses O(1) auxiliary words.

Directional Mergesort++ sorts an array of size n with run-based entropy H (defined for both non-decreasing and decreasing runs) using no more than nH+3n comparisons and 1.5nH+6.5n moves. Excluding the merge buffer of size ⌈n/2⌉, the algorithm uses O(1) auxiliary words.
